explanation:
Falsification attempted against all 7 classes and each fails to eliminate the candidate.

(1) WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL — rejected. "Scope of what an actor is permitted to do, with fail-closed rejection outside that scope" is squarely governance-level semantics, not an implementation detail; the platform's own frozen ADR family (ADR-24-21 through ADR-24-26) treats it at exactly this level, as a peer of Decision Truth and Capability Trust.

(2) MECHANISM_ONLY — rejected for the candidate itself (its definition is normative, not procedural), though this is where the live implementation actually lands: today's only *enforced* representation is a scattered role-string check (`req.authUser.role !== 'ADMIN'`) repeated across 36+ route files (e.g. server/routes/admin.routes.ts:56-388) plus a single per-event signed predicate (PromotionAttestationPredicate) for quarantine promotion. Neither is a durable, canonical "authority" object — both are HOW a specific check is done at a specific call site, not a governed WHAT.

(3) ALREADY_REPRESENTED — tested against three candidate representations and FAILS the lossless reuse test for all three (see lossless_reuse_test). Closest match, ADR-24-21's AuthorityEvidenceArtifact/TrustDomainArtifact/TrustAnchorArtifact/TrustDelegationArtifact, is explicitly logged by the platform's own operational proof registry as `"package_class": "RETIRED_CANDIDATE"`, `"module_role": "UNWIRED_ACTOR_TRUST_MODEL"`, `"proof_status": "UNPROVEN"` with `"proof_reason": "TEST_EXISTS_BUT_IS_NOT_EXECUTED"` (docs/architecture/architecture-authority-map.jsonc, entry id "mps-governance-actor-trust", ~lines 866-880), and its compliance rule ACT-21-I1 is a stub that unconditionally returns `passed: true` with `evidence: []` regardless of input (packages/mps-compliance/src/validators/ACT_21_I1.ts:8-16). Nothing outside its own package/tests constructs an ActorArtifact/AuthorityEvidenceArtifact. A server/routes/governance.routes.ts comment (lines ~213-215) confirms individual actor-level, non-repudiable authority ("Level 3") is "a separate architecture-convergence track, not started."

(4) SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE — rejected. Capability (ADR-24-26) explicitly disclaims this role: "Capability beskriver vad som kan göras, inte vem som får göra det" (docs/architecture/ADR-24-26-Capability-Trust-Connector.md:48), and CapabilityCertificationArtifact takes AuthorityEvidenceArtifact as an external reference (CAP-26-I12, same file line 163-164) rather than reimplementing authority — the platform's own design treats Capability and Authority as distinct. Decision (mps-decision-governance) governs lineage/content of a decision, not the actor's standing to make it. No overlapping candidate found.

(5) DERIVABLE — rejected. The live RBAC role assignment is mutable, overwritten state in the user/session store, not an append-only ledger; there is no reproducible way to reconstruct "what actor X was permitted to do, under what scope, granted by whom, at time T" after a role change. This is the opposite of the deterministic, replay-compatible reconstruction the platform requires elsewhere (e.g. C-05 replay determinism in ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md §7).

(6) NOT_TECHNOLOGY_INDEPENDENT — rejected. Actor permission-scope semantics are independent of any LLM, risk-model, or forecasting technology choice; nothing about Authority would disappear under such a swap.

(7) NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_GOVERNED — rejected. ADR-24-21 is referenced as a shared dependency by five sibling ADRs (24-22 Signature/Attestation, 24-24 Retention, 24-25 Execution Identity, 24-26 Capability Trust, and indirectly 24-19 Workflow) via AuthorityEvidenceArtifact, which is the classic signature of a concept needing its own lifecycle/identity rather than being folded as an attribute onto one specific artifact type.

Because none of the 7 falsification classes eliminates the candidate, and because the one existing design that matches it (ADR-24-21) is present only as an orphaned, unproven, unenforced schema — not a live governing source of truth — the candidate survives as CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES / TRUE_GAP. Note this is a qualified gap: the *semantic design* for Authority already exists on paper (ADR-24-21 + packages/mps-governance/src/actors/*.ts) and is even absent from the current authority chain (docs/architecture/README.md lists neither ADR-24-21 nor any Actor/Trust/Authority document in its §1 "current normative" or §3 "active domain contracts" tables, and ADR-24-21's stated constitutional grounding, MIMER-20-I8 "Explicit Mutation Authority" in ADR-24-20-Constitution.md:96-97, is itself HISTORICAL/superseded). So the true gap is as much a governance-recognition gap (nothing currently anchors Authority under the live constitution) as a code gap.

governance_questions_answered.explanation: ADR-24-21's AuthorityEvidenceArtifact schema models this, but no live code path constructs or checks one (packages/mps-compliance/src/validators/ACT_21_I1.ts:8-16 is a stub returning passed:true unconditionally); the only live checks are per-route RBAC role strings (server/routes/admin.routes.ts) with no canonical 'why permitted' artifact.
governance_questions_answered.question: What permitted a given actor to take a given action, as opposed to merely being able to?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: TrustDomainArtifact scope/constraints exist only as a type definition; its proof test (packages/mps-governance/tests/ADR23Compliance.test.ts) is logged as NO_MATCHING_VITEST_PROJECT_INCLUDE / UNPROVEN in architecture-authority-map.jsonc, i.e. never executed, so no boundary-rejection behavior is verified to exist.
governance_questions_answered.question: What is the boundary of what was permitted, and how would an attempt outside that boundary be recognized and rejected?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: For ADR-24-21 nothing populates a grant record at runtime. The narrower PromotionAttestationPredicate path (packages/mimers-brunn-core/src/governance/DatasetApproval.ts:30-38) does bind approver_actor_id/approver_role under a server-side Ed25519 signature, but that is a different, narrower representation than AuthorityEvidenceArtifact, scoped to one action type, and explicitly lacks per-actor non-repudiation per the code's own comment.
governance_questions_answered.question: Who or what granted the permission, and can that grant be traced and verified after the fact?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: TrustDelegationArtifact (delegator/delegatee/scope/activation/expiration/revocation) and ActorLifecycleArtifact (...→REVOKED) exist only as unused TypeScript interfaces (packages/mps-governance/src/actors/TrustDelegationArtifact.ts, ActorLifecycleArtifact.ts); the live system's only 'revocation' is overwriting a mutable role field in the user store, which is not an auditable, versioned artifact.
governance_questions_answered.question: Can the permission be revoked, delegated, or scoped to a sub-actor?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: No live representation keeps these separate: PromotionAttestationPredicate fuses the authorization grant and the evidence of its exercise into one signed per-event object rather than modeling Authority and Evidence as distinct, independently referenceable artifacts as the candidate's own definition requires.
governance_questions_answered.question: Does the system distinguish 'permitted' from 'physically possible' and from 'evidenced as having happened'?

minimum_semantic_delta: A live, independently-governed, fail-closed AuthorityEvidence artifact family (actor, scope/trust-domain, grantor/delegation chain, revocation) that at least one real mutation path must consult and that is referenced, not reimplemented, by Capability/Decision/Evidence pathways. Concretely: (a) formally anchor Authority under the current constitution — ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md today says nothing about actors/authority, so ADR-24-21 must be reconciled into or re-issued under the live authority chain (docs/architecture/README.md) rather than left orphaned under the superseded ADR-24-20; (b) wire at least one real authorization decision (e.g. quarantine promotion, or the ADMIN-role route checks) to construct and verify a genuine AuthorityEvidenceArtifact instead of a bare role string, replacing the stub ACT_21_I1 validator with a real check; (c) get the existing but unexecuted proof lane (packages/mps-governance/tests/ADR23Compliance.test.ts) running and its proof_status moved from UNPROVEN to PROVEN in architecture-authority-map.jsonc. Because none of this exists live today (only inert type definitions and a rubber-stamp validator), adopting it is effectively adopting a new, previously-unenforced core artifact family into the kernel, not merely renaming or attribute-binding an existing one.
negative_findings: ADR-24-21's full Actor/Trust/Authority schema exists in both ADR prose and TypeScript interfaces, but is provably unenforced: its own compliance rule is a stub, its proof test is not wired into any executed vitest project, and no code outside its own package constructs its artifacts.

The candidate's near-namesake concept 'Authority' is already in live use in this codebase, but only as a classification label on existing artifact TYPES (decision/approval/policy/capability_grant/...) via AUTHORITY_ARTIFACT_TYPES — a different, narrower semantic than 'scope of what an actor may do,' so its presence does not satisfy the candidate.

ADR-24-21 (Actor/Authority) is completely absent from docs/architecture/README.md's authority-chain index, unlike ADR-24-26 (Capability), which is at least cross-referenced from adjacent frozen material — Authority-as-documented is architecturally orphaned even relative to its own sibling ADRs.
semantic_conflicts: ADR-24-21 (orphaned, historical constitutional grounding) vs ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md (current constitution, silent on actor/authority) — a live semantic conflict/gap in the authority chain itself that any AUTHORITY kernel decision must resolve before ADR-24-21 can be cited as canonical.
